items.title: Ensuring Effective and Efficient Agency Logging and Network Visibility to Defend Against Evolving Cyber Threats
items.summary: Replaces M-21-31's 'log nearly everything' model with a risk-based one built on a CISA Logging Reference Architecture (LRA, published Aug 20, 2026). Two goals: continuous event monitoring (logs searchable for at least 6 months) and threat hunting and forensics (retrievable for at least 12 months). Agencies submit a logging plan, then climb a five-element maturity model (levels 0–4) on a fixed schedule from LRA publication. Decentralized architectures are allowed if the SOC can get the data. OT and IoT are in scope where they're part of an agency information system.
items.forYou: The most urgent item on this site. The logging plan is due November 18, 2026, and IT Ops owns most of what it describes: log sources, collection pipeline, normalization, retention tiers, integrity controls and access. The CISO signs; you'll write most of it.

actions.text: Submit DFC's logging plan to OMB and CISA (CyberScope, using CISA's LRA plan template): source coverage, data flow, normalization, retention, integrity protections, access controls and validation.
Configure retention: security logs actively searchable for at least 6 months and retrievable for at least 12 months.
Reach logging maturity Level 1 under the LRA.
Reach logging maturity Level 2.
Reach logging maturity Level 3.
Inventory OT and IoT devices (badge readers, cameras, building controls, printers) that are part of agency information systems and decide their logging path.

items.summary: OMB's civilian playbook for EO 14412: a five-phase migration from 2026 through 2035, and an agency PQC Migration Plan to OMB and ONCD within about 120 days. items.title: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk
items.summary: Replaces severity-only patch deadlines with risk-based prioritization on four factors: asset exposure, KEV status, exploit automation, and post-exploitation technical impact. The result is remediation windows of 3, 14 or 60 days, or deferral to the next system upgrade. Agency policies had to align by August 2026, and remediation on the new timelines starts December 7, 2026. CDM asset reporting expands to cover all networked assets, printers included, with every IP address, including private RFC 1918/4193 ranges.
items.forYou: This rewrites your patching SLAs. Your vulnerability workflow, ticket priorities and any contractor SLA that says '15/30 days for critical/high' need to switch to BOD 26-04 windows by December 7. The printer and private-IP reporting requirement is the sleeper: plenty of CDM feeds don't do that today.

actions.text: Confirm DFC's vulnerability-management policy was updated to BOD 26-04.
Start evaluating and remediating on BOD 26-04 risk-based windows (3/14/60 days or next upgrade). Update ticket priorities and runbooks.
Align contractor SLAs and O&M task orders that hard-code BOD 19-02/22-01 timelines with BOD 26-04 windows.
Make sure CDM reporting covers all networked assets, printers included, with all associated IPs (including RFC 1918/4193).

items.title: Mitigating Risk From End-of-Support Edge Devices
items.summary: Agencies must get end-of-support (EOS) edge devices (firewalls, routers, switches, VPN concentrators, load balancers, wireless controllers) off their networks. Update supported devices running EOS software immediately. Inventory devices on CISA's EOS Edge Device List (3 months). Start removing devices that were already EOS (12 months). Finish removal (18 months). Run continuous discovery with a rolling 12-month EOS forecast (24 months).
items.forYou: Squarely an IT Ops item. Network and perimeter hardware is your refresh budget. The February 5, 2027 milestone is under three months away. If removal isn't funded, raise it now, before the next budget cycle closes.

actions.text: Update vendor-supported edge devices that are running EOS software or firmware.
Inventory edge devices on CISA's EOS Edge Device List and report to CISA (template).
Begin removing and replacing devices that were EOS when the directive was issued.
Complete removal of all identified EOS edge devices and report to CISA.
Stand up continuous edge-device discovery and a rolling inventory of devices going EOS within 12 months.
Put funded replacement of EOS edge devices into the FY27/FY28 budget request.

items.forYou: If DFC runs M365 (or Google Workspace), your tenant configs are continuously graded by CISA. Drift from a mandatory baseline is a finding, so keep SCuBA results in your weekly ops review.

actions.text: Keep the in-scope cloud tenant inventory current with CISA.
Run SCuBA assessments continuously and report to CISA.
Hold mandatory SCuBA configurations and implement new mandatory baselines on CISA's timelines.
